newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates slip to three percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates slip to three percent.

text.p: German call money rates slipped to around three percent on Friday as traders said they were ahead in their monthly reserve holdings, prompting many to try an unload some funds before the weekend.
"At the moment there seems to be enough liquidity," said one dealer, adding however that it was a bit premature to say where rates might move this afternoon.
The bulk of trades was conducted at around three percent on Friday morning, down from Thursday morning's 3.00/05 percent range.
Although holdings at the Bundesbank slipped to 41.4 billion marks on Thursday from Wednesday's 42.1 billion marks, dealers still said there was enough to go around at the moment.
"The reserve numbers look pretty good right now, and so some people are still trying to get rid of some funds ahead of the weekend."
Call money rates are now quite close the Bundesbank's key money market rate, the repo, kept at three percent since August. For next week, dealers said rates could drift slightly higher again however.
On average, banks' monthly holdings were steady at 41.1 billion marks. Lombard borrowings at the 4.50 percent emergency borrowing rate stood at 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.06133 percent on Friday compared with 3.07425 percent on Thursday
